title: cross-functional-roadmap-sync-prep-mar-2026-dylan-personal-notes
body:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment (Product + Eng + Applied ML)
Date: Mar 05 2026 (sync)  prep notes / personal scratchpad
Owner: Dylan Chen (Product PM)
Attendees (expected): Asha (Eng, serving-runtime), Maya (Applied ML), Raj (Infra/Platform), John (Product), + possible SRE rep
Goals for sync:
- Align on priorities for H1 features that impact inference economics (batching/caching, quantized model support, fallback routing)
- Surface hard dependencies and capacity constraints for Dedicated and Private launches
- Agree on decision points and owners for experiment rollouts (A/B for quantized model variants)
Quick context / what I want out of this meeting:
- Confirm which features must ship for Dedicated beta vs can be postponed to Q2
- Lock on go/no-go criteria for model quantization at 8-bit for customer-facing routes
- Get concrete bandwidth estimates from Eng + Applied ML for rolling experiments
Agenda (30–45m):
1) 5m — Quick state: product roadmap highlights & customer asks (me)
2) 10m — Eng constraints: capacity, major infra work, timeline (Asha)
3) 10m — Applied ML: model quality baseline, regression risk, eval plan (Maya)
4) 10m — Dependencies & decisions: what needs cross-team commitment
5) 5–10m — Actions + owners + due dates
Notes / talking points to surface:
- Customer pressure: two pilot customers asked for private deployment w/ 8-bit quantized models and 99th percentile latency < 120ms (they're willing to sign for Dedicated). Need clarity: do we guarantee quantized model parity? (Maya: likely some evals)
- Batching strategy: current runtime batching improvements should reduce token cost by ~20% for chat-heavy workloads — need Eng to confirm when steady-state perf lands in Dedicated images
- KV cache TTL defaults (product wants longer TTL for cost savings) — SRE concerns about mem usage on Dedicated clusters (Raj)
- Rollout policy: prefer canary on small pilot orgs + automatic rollback on quality regression metrics (we have tooling in Console but need to define thresholds)
Open questions / risks:
- Risk: Quantization regressions on instruction-following tasks — need an eval suite and guardrails before customer rollout
- Risk: Dedicated capacity availability in EU region for private customers in April (possible delay)
- Who owns customer communication if we need to slip timeline? (product owns messaging, Eng + Applied ML provide timing)
Decision requests (what I want decided during/after this sync):
- D1: Ship Dedicated beta with quantized model support as opt-in ONLY (on-by-default = NO). Owner: Product (me) — due: Mar 12
- D2: Define A/B experiment for 8-bit quantization with rollback threshold of 2% delta on BLEU/ROUGE or equivalent eval metrics; owner: Maya — due: Mar 10
- D3: KV cache default TTL set to 30m for Dedicated; SRE to provide mem impact estimate by Mar 9 (owner: Raj)
Action items (initial, assignable):
- A1: Maya to run quantization regression suite (baseline + instruction-following prompts) and surface top 5 failure modes; deliverable: short report + sample prompts. Due: Mar 9
- A2: Asha to provide Dedicated image release timeline (contains batching/runtime perf improvements) + throughput numbers for 4 common request profiles. Due: Mar 11
- A3: Raj to run capacity check for EU Dedicated clusters and propose mitigation (burst capacity plan). Due: Mar 10
- A4: John to draft customer-facing beta notes (opt-in quantization + support caveats). Due: Mar 12
- A5: Dylan (me) to synthesize meeting notes + update Confluence roadmap with agreed scope. Due: Mar 13
Follow-ups / personal TODOs before sync:
- Build quick slide (1–2) with: roadmap bullets, customer asks, and clear list of decisions we need — to keep meeting tight
- Prepare 2–3 sample prompts to illustrate quantization regressions (if Maya needs examples)
- Ping SRE channel about memory telemetry for KV cache
Potential blockers to escalate to execs:
- If EU Dedicated capacity can't be committed for April pilots, we may need to push pilot customers or offer hosted fallback — escalate to VP Eng
- If quantization regressions exceed our rollback threshold in early experiments, we'll need additional ML engineering bandwidth to fix — may require reprioritizing research tickets
Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Keep tone collaborative in meeting; don't push for final decisions without Eng/ML buy-in
- If we get pushback on TTL or defaults, propose a pilot with 1–2 customers first
- Make sure we capture exact SLO changes if we adjust default routing to quantized variants (affects docs + pricing)
Quick links / references:
- Confluence roadmap (linked above)
- JIRA-4567 (Dedicated beta plan)
- PR: inference-runtime #512 (batching perf)
--end of notes--
